text:
marie: ran an nsys trace on the failing kv-batcher run, attaching the quick notes below. saw weird gaps where host memcpy seems to wait for CPU scheduling before the copy engine kicks in.
aj: can you paste the timeline snippet?
marie: here's the relevant waterfall I pulled from Nsight Systems:
```
# timeline excerpt (annotated)
stream 0: [kernel] sgemm_v2         5.1ms
stream 2: [memcpy HtoD]            2.3ms  (queued after host thread wake)
stream 0: [kernel] softmax_kv       1.8ms
cpu  : host thread sleeping -> wake (1.2ms gap) -> enqueue memcpy
```

marie: the memcpy is asynchronous but appears serialized because the host thread wakes late and enqueues it on the default stream, so copy engine doesn't overlap with sgemm on stream 0.
ravi: hmm, default stream semantics could be the culprit. are we using implicit synchronization anywhere?
marie: not intentionally. batcher uses a small helper thread that builds IO vectors and posts cudaMemcpyAsync for each KV chunk. suspect wake latency + many tiny memcpy calls.
juan: how small are the memcpys? size distribution?
marie: mostly 16KB-128KB per entry, ~200 entries per request at peak. lots of syscall overhead and scheduler churn.
sophia: that could explain the CPU scheduling gap — thread does a loop of `cudaMemcpyAsync` + `std::this_thread::yield()` in our current batcher.
aj: can we coalesce into fewer larger pinned host buffers?
marie: tried coalescing in a dev branch: single buffer per request + one cudaMemcpyAsync -> overlap improved. nsight shows copy engine active during kernel on stream 0, latency per request down 18%.
perf-bot: perf regression alert: service-3 saw 12% p50 increase last week correlated with the new small-batch KV rollout.
juan: nice catch. what's the repro trace command?
marie: `nsys profile -o kvtrace --trace=cuda,osrt,cuda_memcpy -f true --sample=none --capture-range=nvtx` then open in Nsight Systems. also captured perfetto for CPU wake stacks.
ravi: aside from coalescing, two quick experiments: 1) use cudaStreamCreateWithPriority for hostcopy stream so copy engine gets higher priority, 2) switch to pinned pool and use batched copy (single big HtoD).
sophia: remember pinned allocations increase memory pressure on the host, we should measure.
aj: any kernel selection interplay? if kernels move to a different stream or use exclusive compute, we might get better overlap without touching batcher.
marie: we also saw a kernel selector fallback on some sequences which pushed sgemm to a slower kernel (higher occupancy) increasing compute time and reducing opportunities to hide memcpy. two simultaneous regressions compounded.
juan: stack trace from perfetto for the host thread wake?
marie: perfetto showed `futex` wake then ~900us to `enqueue_memcpy` due to scheduling latency under load, then another ~300us in syscall. total ~1.2ms gap before memcpy command reaches CUDA driver.
ravi: actionable list: coalesce small memcpys in batcher (short-term), try prioritized stream for hostcopy (short-term), add NVTX around enqueue to correlate driver latency (short/med), and open an experiment to push more KV fetch work to a dedicated I/O thread pool to avoid preemption.
sophia: +add a canary that toggles coalescing at runtime so we can A/B the effect without full rollout.
aj: also add test traces in CI with synthetic microbatch shapes we saw in prod (200 entries of 32KB) and assert p50 doesn't regress >5%.
marie: will push a small coalesce patch to `kv-batcher/coalesce-hostcopy` and attach a trace. expecting ~10-20% p50 perf recovery.
juan: thanks — if the coalescing helps we'll still need the kernel-selection fix to reclaim the rest.
perf-bot: note: schedule a follow-up perf run once coalesce branch is live. tag @sre for load-profile alignment.
marie: uploaded a short nsys .qdrep to the PR and a perfetto trace link. leaving the trace notes in the PR description.
aj: LGTM, pls include the NVTX regions and make sure pinned pool is opt-in.
ravi: one more thought: consider using cudaMemcpyAsync with cudaMemcpyHostToDevice on a stream created with `cudaStreamAttachMemAsync` semantics when combined with `cudaMemAdvise` — might reduce visible host-side latency in some kernels. worth an experiment.
sophia: updated the ticket with the remediation plan and risks. I'll coordinate the canary rollout.
marie: thanks all — will follow up with before/after traces in this thread. :thumbsup:
